messages:
Eli J.: Quick check-in on the planned fission of the runtime hotpath into `ingest/transform/serve`. I posted a short sketch in the docs folder. Want to call out operational assumptions before we cutover.
Marta P.: skimmed. main assumption that worries me: we rely on eventual cache consistency during reads. need an explicit prefill and a read-sticky window.
Corey L.: agreed. propose: prefill KV from snapshot + warm pool with synthetic traffic at 10% qps for 20m. Also disable autoscale burst for first 12h.
Eli J.: good. on API contracts: add `schema_version` header and runtime validator that returns 412 for mismatches. metric `schema_mismatch` should trigger a canary rollback.
Marta P.: rollout cadence suggestion: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% -> 35% over 72h, with 30-45m gating windows. per-tenant opt-in for top-10 tenants.
Corey L.: fallback policy: route to monolith shim when p95 > 600ms for 20m OR error_rate > 0.5% for 10m. We can wire router to model-variant fallback already in place.
deploy-bot: CI created `runtime-fission-canary`. Manual trigger only. Logs: https://ci.internal/job/runtime-fission-canary/321
Eli J.: ops runbook excerpt:
```
- pre-cutover: snapshot KV, warm workers, notify top tenants
- canary: follow cadence, run replay of last 6h traffic against canary
- backfill: dual-write for 14 days, idempotent backfill job rate-limited to 200r/s
- rollback: flip routing to shim, mark canary failed, begin investigation
```
Marta P.: test matrix: contract tests, golden replay, chaos test (kill cache node), memory leak smoke. QA will run nightly against canary.
Corey L.: debt-paydown: create deprecation ticket for old endpoints, assign owner, remove shim after 60 days if stable. scoreboard updates weekly in #architecture.
Eli J.: timeline: PR this week, staging canary next Tue, prod canary 2 weeks later. Please ack blockers by EOD. :thumbsup:
